From 25537d71e2d007faf42a244a75e5a2bb7c356234 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2021 17:12:15 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net: Allow NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX if IP_CSUM && IPV6_CSUM

Cited patch below blocked the TLS TX device offload unless HW_CSUM
is set. This broke devices that use IP_CSUM && IP6_CSUM.
Here we fix it.

Note that the single HW_TLS_TX feature flag indicates support for
both IPv4/6, hence it should still be disabled in case only one of
(IP_CSUM | IPV6_CSUM) is set.

Fixes: ae0b04b238e2 ("net: Disable NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX when HW_CSUM is disabled")
Signed-off-by: Tariq Toukan <tariqt@nvidia.com>
Reported-by: Rohit Maheshwari <rohitm@chelsio.com>
Reviewed-by: Maxim Mikityanskiy <maximmi@mellanox.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20210114151215.7061-1-tariqt@nvidia.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/core/dev.c b/net/core/dev.c
index 0071a11a6dc3..c360bb5367e2 100644
--- a/net/core/dev.c
+++ b/net/core/dev.c
@@ -9661,9 +9661,15 @@ static netdev_features_t netdev_fix_features(struct net_device *dev,
 		}
 	}
 
-	if ((features & NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX) && !(features & NETIF_F_HW_CSUM)) {
-		netdev_dbg(dev, "Dropping TLS TX HW offload feature since no CSUM feature.\n");
-		features &= ~NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX;
+	if (features & NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX) {
+		bool ip_csum = (features & (NETIF_F_IP_CSUM | NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM)) ==
+			(NETIF_F_IP_CSUM | NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM);
+		bool hw_csum = features & NETIF_F_HW_CSUM;
+
+		if (!ip_csum && !hw_csum) {
+			netdev_dbg(dev, "Dropping TLS TX HW offload feature since no CSUM feature.\n");
+			features &= ~NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX;
+		}
 	}
 
 	return features;
-- 
2.25.1



diff --git a/Documentation/networking/tls-offload.rst b/Documentation/networking/tls-offload.rst
index 0f55c6d540f9..9af3334d9ad0 100644
--- a/Documentation/networking/tls-offload.rst
+++ b/Documentation/networking/tls-offload.rst
@@ -530,7 +530,7 @@ TLS device feature flags only control adding of new TLS connection
 offloads, old connections will remain active after flags are cleared.
 
 TLS encryption cannot be offloaded to devices without checksum calculation
-offload. Hence, TLS TX device feature flag requires NETIF_F_HW_CSUM being set.
+offload. Hence, TLS TX device feature flag requires TX csum offload being set.
 Disabling the latter implies clearing the former. Disabling TX checksum offload
 should not affect old connections, and drivers should make sure checksum
 calculation does not break for them.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `net/core/dev.c`**
   - The logic for determining whether to drop the `NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX` feature has been modified. 
   - The previous condition that dropped the `NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX` feature if `NETIF_F_HW_CSUM` was not set has been changed. 
   - Now, the feature will only be dropped if neither `NETIF_F_IP_CSUM` nor `NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM` is set, allowing for the use of `NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX` when either IP checksum feature is enabled, even if hardware checksum is not.

2. **File: `Documentation/networking/tls-offload.rst`**
   - The documentation has been updated to reflect the new condition for the `NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX` feature. 
   - The requirement for the TLS TX device feature flag has been changed from requiring `NETIF_F_HW_CSUM` to requiring "TX checksum offload" to be set, clarifying that it can now work with IP checksum features.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The changes in `net/core/dev.c` directly address the issue raised in the documentation regarding the conditions under which the `NETIF_F_HW_TLS_TX` feature can be enabled. 
- The modification in the code allows for greater flexibility by permitting the TLS TX offload feature to be active when either IP checksum feature is enabled, which was not possible before due to the stricter requirement of hardware checksum.
- The documentation update ensures that users and developers are aware of the new logic implemented in the code, providing clarity on the conditions for enabling TLS TX offload. This relationship between the code and documentation ensures that both are aligned and accurately reflect the current functionality.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **Documentation/networking/tls-offload.rst**
   - The text was modified to clarify that the TLS TX device feature flag requires TX checksum offload to be set, rather than specifically requiring the NETIF_F_HW_CSUM feature. This change reflects the broader requirement that either IP_CSUM or IPV6_CSUM must be enabled for TLS TX offload to be applicable.

2. **net/core/dev.c**
   - The logic for determining whether to drop the TLS TX hardware offload feature was updated. 
   - The previous condition that dropped the feature if `NETIF_F_HW_CSUM` was not set was replaced with a new condition that checks if both `NETIF_F_IP_CSUM` and `NETIF_F_IPV6_CSUM` are not set. 
   - If neither of these checksum features is enabled, the TLS TX offload feature is dropped, allowing for devices that support either IP_CSUM or IPV6_CSUM to still utilize TLS TX offload.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The changes in the documentation and the code are closely related. The documentation update provides context for the code modification by clarifying the conditions under which TLS TX offload can be enabled. The code change implements this clarification by allowing the TLS TX feature to remain enabled if either IP_CSUM or IPV6_CSUM is set, rather than requiring the more restrictive HW_CSUM. This ensures that devices that support checksum offloading for either IPv4 or IPv6 can still benefit from TLS offload, addressing the issue that arose from the previous patch.
